newsitem.title: FRANCE: Early French poll will not delay EMU -de Silguy.
newsitem.headline: Early French poll will not delay EMU -de Silguy.

text.p: European Union Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Friday that a French decision to stage early general elections would not alter the timetable for European monetary union.
"The european calendar is unaffected by national calendars," de Silguy said in an interview on French television LCI.
"The (EMU) calendar will be respected. On January 1, 1999, the euro will be the currency of Europe."

Key leaders of France's centre-right majority have been encouraging President Jacques Chirac to call early elections rather than wait until March 1998, as currently scheduled. Others have suggested reshuffling the cabinet.
French media reports said Chirac would spend the weekend considering such a move and would make his decision known next week.
